reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega be a measurable space, E a complete real inner-product normed space equipped with a measurable space equal to its Borel structure, mu a measure on Omega, and F an NNReal-indexed filtration. Let B:[0,infinity) x Omega -> E be a standard Brownian motion with F: B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments over any finite collection of disjoint half-open time intervals are jointly independent; each continuous real linear functional applied to an increment from s to t, s<t, is centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)*||ell||^2; B has continuous paths mu-almost everywhere; B is strongly F-adapted; and for s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of F_s. For every continuous linear functional ell:E->R of operator norm 1, the real process W(t,omega)=ell(B(t,omega)) is Brownian with filtration F under mu. Precisely, W satisfies ProbabilityTheory.IsBrownianReal, is strongly F-adapted, and for every s<=t its increment W(t)-W(s) is independent of F_s. No finite-measure, finite-dimensional, separability, or additional usual-conditions hypothesis appears. The scalar IsBrownianReal condition means that every finite collection of time evaluations has the centered Gaussian law with covariance min(s,t), and sample paths are almost surely continuous. Its zero-at-time-zero requirement follows only almost surely from that law; the vector input here additionally has B(0,omega)=0 pointwise.
objects: Omega, real Hilbert space E with Borel measurable structure, mu, F, E-valued B, continuous linear functional ell, projected real process W.
domains: Time NNReal; Omega arbitrary measurable type; E complete real inner-product space; ell in StrongDual R E.
quantifiers: For every such space, measure, filtration and B, if B has the specified standard Brownian-with-filtration property, then for every ell with norm 1 the projected process has the real Brownian-with-filtration property.
assumptions: Standard Brownian-with-filtration property for B; ||ell||=1; declared completeness and Borel hypotheses on E.
conclusion: W=ell composed with B satisfies IsBrownianReal, strong adaptedness, and F_s-independence of all increments from s to t with s<=t. Its finite-dimensional laws are centered Gaussian with covariance min(s,t), and its paths are mu-almost surely continuous.
scopes: All nonnegative times, no fixed horizon. Path continuity in the Brownian property is almost everywhere; starting at zero in the supplied vector Brownian definition is pointwise.
constant_dependencies: Projection uses the given ell and B. Normalization is exactly 1; there is no existential constant.
context_ambiguities: None identified from the supplied statement and definition context.
